title: Business Office Specialist
description:
Tulsa, Oklahoma, United States of America

Extraordinary Care. Extraordinary Careers.

With one of the nation’s largest, most innovative long-term care pharmacy services providers, there is no limit to the growth of your career.

Boomer Solutions of Tulsa, a member of the Guardian family of pharmacies, has an exciting opportunity for you to join our rapidly growing team in Tulsa, Oklahoma.

Why Boomer Solutions of Tulsa? We’re reimagining medication management and transforming care.

Who We Are and What We’re About:

Our core focus is delivering customized medication management solutions to support healthcare organizations serving seniors and individuals with complex care needs. With our comprehensive suite of tech-enabled pharmacy services and a dedicated team of professionals committed to enriching the lives of those we serve, we are redefining how pharmacy care is delivered.

We offer an opportunity to learn and grow your career in a fast-paced, diverse, and inclusive environment. If you are looking for a challenging, team-oriented environment in which you can put your expertise to work, then this is the place for you.

As a supporting member to the local management team, assists in day-to-day financial support and operations of the pharmacy by providing assistance in monitoring of financial management, human resources and general administrative support as well as performing data and research assistance.

ATTRIBUTES REQUIRED:

  • Work Ethic/Integrity – must possess intrinsic drive to excel coupled with values in line with company philosophy.
  • Leadership – ability to lead project teams to deadlines, while maintaining strong team orientation
  • Relational – ability to build relationships with business unit management and become “trusted advisor.”
  • Strategy and Planning – ability to think ahead, plan and manage time efficiently.
  • Problem Solving – ability to analyze causes and solve problems at both a strategic and functional level.
  • Team Oriented – ability to work effectively and collaboratively with all team members.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS (could include, but not limited to the following):

Financial Support:

  • Perform daily / weekly functions to include: daily deposits, payment postings, coding of invoices, and processing daily US Mail.
  • Prepare ad-hoc system & AR reporting and research as requested by management team and support.
  • Assist in collecting and managing reports related to credit card and private pay customers, ensuring process is efficient and accurate.
  • Manage deposits, credit cards, and all cash related activities through Regions, Etactics, and BillerXchange
  • As needed Assist with billing and collections function to ensure a high level of customer service is maintained and collection targets achieved by reviewing accounts and taking proactive approach to minimize AR risk.
  • Manage and review the approval process for all expenses and invoices; ensure bills are being correctly submitted to Workday – coded accurately prior to submission for DFA approval.
  • Maintain the AP log and assist in accrual information for month end reporting.
  • Other essential functions and duties may be assigned as needed.

Administrative (applicable as needed by location) :

  • Prepare for, greet, and direct visitors to the pharmacy.
  • Maintain calendars for all key dates and deadlines related to pharmacy events and the financial management of business.
  • Help with preparations for, and assist with, Family Night for new facilities.
  • Assist management with building and maintenance issues.
  • Manage the ordering of office supplies and monitor expenses within budget.
  • Provide administrative support to senior leadership as needed.
  • Other functions and duties may be assigned as needed.

Human Capital (in the absence of onsite HR support):

  • Manage the candidate flow in the applicant tracking system, completing phone screens with candidates, and scheduling interviews for the candidate and hiring supervisor.
  • Initiate steps in applicant tracking system to move candidate through background and hire once a hiring decision has been made by the hiring supervisor.
  • Oversee and manage local on-boarding of new employees including all steps to complete the HRIS transmission as required by Atlanta support staff.
  • Ensuring all relevant benefits are communicated effectively and timely to employees including open enrollment deadlines.
  • Train new employees on pharmacy policies, procedures, and processes
  • Other functions and duties may be assigned as needed.


EDUCATION AND/OR CERTIFICATIONS

  • High School Diploma or GED required; Bachelor's Degree (Math, English, Economics, Business, Computer Science, or similar) preferred
  • Pharmacy Technician certification or ability to obtain Trainee’s license (per state requirements) preferred


SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3+ years’ experience in a bookkeeping/analytical position
  • Excellent MS Office skills; emphasis on Excel expertise; working knowledge of pharmacy billing/operating system
  • Working knowledge of accounting principles required with strong analytical skills
  • Confidentiality: ability to use exercise good judgment and maintain confidential information
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills
  • Ability to work in a demanding fast paced environment
  • Ability to work independently and deliver to deadlines
  • Ability to solve problems with minimal direction
  • Great attention to detail and accuracy
  • Quality minded; motivated to seek out errors and inquire when something appears inaccurate.


WORK ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the job.

  • The noise level in the work environment is usually low to moderate.
  • Due to the collaborative nature of the business and the need to service customers, the employee must be able to interact effectively with others in an office environment, manage conflict, and handle stressful situations and deadlines.
  • Requires desk work in office environment.
  • Requires up to 0-20% travel, by air and ground
  • Ability to work flexible hours

What We Offer:

Guardian provides employees with a comprehensive Total Rewards package, supporting our core value of, “Treat others as you would like to be treated.”

Compensation & Financial

  • Competitive pay
  • 401(k) with company match

Family, Health & Insurance Benefits (Full-Time employees working 30+ hours/week only)

  • Medical, Dental and Vision
  • Health Savings Accounts and Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Company-paid Basic Life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment
  • Company-paid Long-Term Disability and optional Short-Term Disability
  • Voluntary Employee and Dependent Life, Accident and Critical Illness
  • Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts

Wellbeing

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Guardian Angels (Employee assistance fund)

Time Off

  • Paid holidays and sick days
  • Generous vacation benefits based on years of service

The Guardian Difference

Our clients require pharmacy services that aren’t “cookie cutter.” That’s why every Guardian pharmacy is locally operated and empowered with the autonomy to tailor their business to meet their clients’ needs.

Our corporate support offices, based in Atlanta, Ga., provide services such as human resources, business intelligence, legal, and marketing to promote the success of each Guardian location.

Regardless of your role at Guardian, your voice and talents matter. Because healthcare is an ever-changing industry, we encourage innovative thinking, intellectual curiosity, and diverse viewpoints to ensure we stay competitive in today’s dynamic business environment.

At Guardian, we are dedicated to fostering and advancing a diverse and inclusive workforce.

Join us to discover what your best work truly looks like.

description:

Serving as the first point of contact at a CIBC Kiosk in Costco Warehouses, you’ll proactively engage clients to understand their needs and identify opportunities. You’ll complete sales of Chequing and Savings accounts, and provide high-level information on other products (e.g., mortgages, Investor’s Edge, registered products) within the scope of the agreed product mix with Costco. You’ll refer clients for non-deposit account advice and servicing conversations to the appropriate Banking Centre. You’ll thrive in this role if you are entrepreneurial in nature and comfortable working in a self-managed environment.

At CIBC, we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. To successfully perform the work, you will be on-site full-time.

This role is located inside Costco warehouses with extended hours of business and requires rotational shift work Monday to Sunday between the hours of 7:00 AM and 9:00 PM, based on the warehouse hours. You will be required to work on weekends and some statutory holidays. Commuting between nearby Costco Warehouses is required, as the kiosk location changes.

Understand the full suite of products available at banking centres in order to identify opportunities during conversations with Costco members and make viable introductions to banking centre based colleagues.

Process valid transactions, complete all related documentation on time and obtain authorization as required. Maintain and ensure client confidentiality at all times to ensure compliance with established policies and procedures. Opening or closing the kiosk at the start or end of business hours may be required.

What You Will Do

  • Experience in interacting with customers and acting as their representative within internal teams.

Preferred

What We Offer

title: Staff Product Manager
description:
About Us:

Proofpoint is a global leader in human- and agent-centric cybersecurity. We protect how people, data, and AI agents connect across email, cloud, and collaboration tools. Over 80 of the Fortune 100, 10,000 large enterprises, and millions of smaller organizations trust Proofpoint to stop threats, prevent data loss, and build resilience across their people and AI workflows. Our mission is simple: safeguard the digital world and empower people to work securely and confidently. Join us in our pursuit to defend data and protect people.

How We Work:

At Proofpoint you’ll be part of a global team that breaks barriers to redefine cybersecurity guided by our BRAVE core values:

Bold in how we dream and innovate

Responsive to feedback, challenges and opportunities

Accountable for results and best in class outcomes

Visionary in future focused problem-solving

Exceptional in execution and impact

The Role

Proofpoint is seeking a Staff Product Manager to drive product strategy and execution for a critical area of our enterprise security platform. This is a senior individual contributor role for an experienced product leader who can tackle complex customer and business problems, shape product direction, and drive alignment and execution across multiple teams.

The ideal candidate combines deep product management expertise with strong business acumen, technical credibility, and exceptional product judgment. You have a track record of identifying meaningful customer problems, developing compelling product strategies, influencing senior stakeholders, and delivering solutions that create measurable customer and business value.

In this role, you will partner closely with engineering, design, sales, marketing, customer success, and other Product leaders to translate customer insights and market opportunities into clear product strategies and roadmaps. You will operate with significant autonomy, lead through influence rather than authority, and help raise the quality of product thinking and execution across the organization.

What You'll Do

  • Define and drive the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for a complex and strategically important product area aligned with broader company and platform objectives.

  • Own ambiguous, high-impact product problems that span multiple capabilities, teams, or areas of the customer experience.

  • Develop a deep understanding of customer workflows and the problems they need to solve, serving as a strong voice of the customer throughout the product development process.

  • Partner closely with engineering and design to translate product strategy into clear priorities, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and deliver scalable, enterprise-grade solutions.

  • Translate customer insights, market trends, competitive dynamics, technical opportunities, and business priorities into actionable product strategies and investment recommendations.

  • Engage directly with customers and prospects to uncover unmet needs, validate product direction, and develop a strong understanding of evolving enterprise security challenges.

  • Define and monitor product success metrics, using customer feedback, product analytics, and business performance to guide prioritization

  • Lead product discovery and roadmap planning for your area, communicating priorities, tradeoffs, and expected outcomes to senior stakeholders.

  • Partner with go-to-market teams on positioning, launches, field enablement, adoption

  • Represent the product in strategic customer conversations, executive briefings, analyst discussions, and industry engagements as appropriate.

  • Identify opportunities to partner with the wider organization or external partnerships that accelerate customer value.

What We're Looking for

  • Bachelor's or equivalent degree experience; Masters or MBA preferred

  • 5+ years of product management experience, ideally including significant experience leading complex software products from strategy through execution.

  • Proven experience defining and executing product strategy for enterprise software.

  • Previous experience in large enterprise SaaS providers and cyber-security are desirable.

  • Demonstrated success owning B2B products or product areas from customer discovery and strategy through development, launch, adoption, and optimization.

  • A track record of solving complex and ambiguous product problems across multiple teams and functions.

  • Exceptional product judgment and the ability to translate the highest-value customer problems into differentiated product experiences.

  • Strong ability to influence senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Deep understanding of enterprise customer needs, buying processes, administrative workflows, and the requirements of building products for large organizations.

  • Strong technical aptitude and the ability to engage effectively with engineering on architecture, platform capabilities, technical investments, and tradeoffs.

  • Strong strategic and commercial thinking, with the ability to balance customer value, technical feasibility, competitive differentiation, and business outcomes.

  • Strong analytical skills and experience using customer feedback, market research, competitive insights, and product data to make informed decisions.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to tailor style and content for different audiences.

  • Experience engaging directly with enterprise customers, prospects and partners.

  • A demonstrated ability to mentor and elevate other Product Managers through expertise, collaboration, and example.

Why Proofpoint?

At Proofpoint, we believe that an exceptional career experience includes a comprehensive compensation and benefits package. Here are just a few reasons you’ll love working with us:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Comprehensive benefits

  • Career success on your terms

  • Flexible work environment

  • Annual wellness and community outreach days

  • Always on recognition for your contributions

  • Global collaboration and networking opportunities

Our Culture:

Our culture is rooted in values that inspire belonging, empower purpose and drive success-every day, for everyone.

We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. If you need accommodation during the application or interview process, please reach out to accessibility@proofpoint.com.

How to Apply

Interested? Submit your application along with any supporting information- we can’t wait to hear from you!

ClientLink is a mission-critical wealth management platform that supports portfolio accounting, investment operations, and client servicing across the enterprise. As part of our strategic modernization journey, we are transforming the platform using modern architecture, event-driven integration, cloud-native technologies, and an enterprise AI Engineering Platform that accelerates software delivery through reusable AI capabilities, standardized engineering workflows, and governance.
We are seeking an experienced Principal Technical Lead – AI & Platform Modernization to lead this transformation. This role combines deep technical expertise, people leadership, software architecture, and AI-enabled engineering to deliver the next generation of ClientLink.
As the senior technical leader, you will define the technical vision, lead an engineering team, establish engineering standards, and drive the adoption of AI-enabled software engineering practices that improve delivery velocity, software quality, and developer productivity.

What will you do?

  • Provide strategic technical leadership to successfully execute the ClientLink modernization roadmap and ensure alignment with the organization’s long-term technology strategy.
  • Lead the adoption and governance of the organization’s AI Engineering Platform, establishing a new AI-enabled software engineering model through standardized skills, plugins, workflows, and engineering guardrails.
  • Establish consistent architecture, engineering standards, and modernization practices across multiple workstreams to improve software quality, scalability, security, and maintainability.
  • Build and mentor high-performing engineering teams while driving the adoption of modern software engineering practices, accelerating delivery, and reducing technical debt.

title: Weekend Production Roaster
description:
About Us:

Groundwork Coffee specializes in batch-roasted, certified organic coffees and artisanal teas. From our humble roots as a rare book store and cafe back in 1990, Groundwork would go on to become one of the first certified organic coffee roasters in Southern California, as well as the largest organic coffee roaster in Los Angeles. A truly local pioneer in fair trade and fairly traded coffee and tea sourcing, we remain committed to sustainable business practices, including maintaining direct relationships with growers and importers who promote responsible coffee and tea production. From the ground up, Groundwork is steadfast in its commitment to the values of quality, sustainability and community.

JOB TITLE: Production Roaster

DEPARTMENT: Roastery

DOL STATUS: CLASSIFICATION: Full Time Non-Exempt (gets OT pay)

SCHEDULE(S): Saturday and Sunday, 6 AM-2:30 PM / 2:30 PM 11:00 PM

LOCATION: 539 SE Division Place, Portland, OR 97202

REPORTS TO POSITION: Production Manager

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES: No direct reports.

Position Overview

The Production Roaster follows roasting protocols and profiles to produce roasted coffee within specifications. The Production Roaster is responsible for production roasting and routine maintenance of the production roasters, including but not limited to: operating the production roaster, correctly adhering to blend recipes and profiles, routine maintenance/cleaning, quality control, and data input and management. This position is responsible for self-monitoring quality control and notifying the Production Manager and Quality Control (“QC”)/Quality Assurance (“QA”) department of any roasts that may fall out of specification. The Production Roaster works in a fast-paced environment subject to numerous schedule/ priority changes on short notice.

Role Priorities

  • Roasting coffee. Adhering to the Roast Schedule as determined by the Production Manager, utilizing the Cropster roasting program, to maintain quality control and consistency of roasts.
  • Staying up to date with blend formulas, roast profiles, and changes.
  • Fluency and understanding of roaster operation and maintenance, and Cropster roasting software.
  • Routine roaster maintenance, adhering to the maintenance schedule.
  • Keeping a tidy work area/roasting floor. Regular QC of all roasted coffee.
  • Notifying others when there are discrepancies with roasts, green coffee inventory, or order fulfillment.
  • Conducting Green Coffee and Roasted Coffee inventory counts and maintaining organized inventory on the floor and storage racks.
  • Blending of large quantities of various coffees, as required, and determined by the Production Manager.
  • Checking in with the Production Manager before ending roasting shifts.

Work Environment

Warehouse/Production environment: busy, tight quarters, sometimes stuffy, dusty, ever-present coffee roasting aroma. Noise level is usually moderate but may be loud depending on roasting activity.

Additional Duties

The Production Roaster is a critical role in the operation of Groundwork Coffee and our Production Department. The Production Roaster must be capable of supporting production needs as they increase and decrease based on demand. Additional hours may be necessary, and are expected on an as-needed basis.

Role Qualifications

  • Forklift certification, or the ability to be trained and operate a forklift.
  • Fluency in information systems (Cropster/ Inventory Tools) and Quality Control procedures and protocols
  • Understanding of needs for daily production for a Roasting Facility (packaging, blending, receiving, shipping, etc.)
  • Understanding and fluency of the coffee roasting process
  • Understanding of roast defects and their causes (both sensory and mechanical)
  • Understanding of green and roasted coffee inventory management
  • Ability to maintain records and documents
  • Ability to lift a minimum of 50lbs, and to move 150lbs with proper support.
  • Able to work independently with little or no supervision
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality when needed
  • Commitment to company values and vision
  • Willingness to pitch in wherever needed, especially loading/unloading trucks, and inventory control.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Team Work: Strong, positive, and constructive team player. Reliable, respectful, and detail-oriented.
  • Pressure: Able to maintain focus when operating in a busy, distracting environment. Takes initiative.
  • Flexible/Adaptable: Able to deal skillfully and promptly with new situations. Energized by challenges.
  • Receptive to Feedback: Gains insights from mistakes and is open to and actively seeks feedback.
  • Time Management: Ability to organize and manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Communication: Ability to communicate in a clear verbal manner. Relates well to all kinds of people.
  • Dealing with Ambiguity: Open to change; learns quickly when facing new/unfamiliar tasks or challenges.
  • Planning: Can break down work into process steps; anticipates and adjusts for problems and roadblocks.
  • Problem Solving: Observant, aware. Resourceful, creative problem-solver.
  • Conflict Management: Effectively handles issues and/or complaints without escalating the situation.
  • Approachability: Spends the extra effort to put others at ease. Builds constructive relationships.
  • Presentation Skill: Effective in a variety of formal presentation settings. Commands attention and can manage group processes during the presentation.
  • Strong Customer-Orientation: Can-do, friendly, professional, “Win-Win” attitude.

Physical Demands

This position is very active. Primarily a standing job (sometimes on even and uneven surfaces) within the facility, stooping, bending, twisting, leaning, grasping, and occasional lifting of 50 pounds or more.

Why Groundwork:

We strive to be the best place our employees have ever worked, and to produce the best coffee our customers have ever sipped. As a part of our team, you’ll be working with people who are down-to-earth, friendly, and passionate in a casual, caffeinated, and fun retail environment.

Groundwork Perks:*Benefits are offered to eligible employees and are subject to change.

  • Free Coffee to Take Home: 1 pound Bulk Coffee or ¼ Pound Loose Leaf Tea every other week
  • Employee Discount Program: Discounts on Food, Beverage, & Merchandise
  • Paid Time Off: Sick Hours
  • Commuter Program: Substantially Subsidized Metro Pass

Groundwork is committed to a policy of Equal Employment Opportunity. We recruit, employ, train, compensate, and promote without regard to race, color, age, sex, ancestry, marital status, religion, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, present or past history of mental disability, genetic information, or any other classification protected by state or federal law.

title: Director - Data Platform
description:
Job Description:

The Director of Data Platforms is responsible for leading a function and/or collection of teams within CSI's data engineering organization in the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of secure, scalable, well-governed data platforms and pipelines across CSI's banking and fintech solutions. This position executes the data platform technology vision and organizational plans in conformance with the company's policies and the objectives of senior management, and is responsible for the workload, outputs, and resources within the data engineering function. The Director establishes short- and long-term goals, standards, and processes that align data platform delivery with broader product, analytics, and AI strategies, leads a team of engineering managers, and champions continuous improvement and strong governance across the data lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Organizational Management

  • Directs a department of data engineers, data architects, quality engineers, and other individual contributors to achieve strategic and operational goals for CSI's data platforms.
  • Inspires, coaches, and provides guidance to team members to improve performance, drive accountability, and support achievement of business objectives.
  • Partners with senior leadership on the data platform vision and strategy, helping shape the future-state data engineering organization.
  • Communicates organizational priorities, policy, and strategy clearly across the department.
  • Champions a culture of ownership, initiative, continuous improvement, and strong data stewardship.
  • Upholds all policies and procedures, company culture, and values.

Data Platform Delivery & Engineering Oversight

  • Owns the quality of data pipelines, warehouses, and platforms delivered, and the implementation of standards, methods, metrics, and procedures across the data engineering lifecycle, evaluating and refining as needed with other leaders in the organization.
  • Directs the architecture, performance, and cost management of CSI's Snowflake environment, including warehouse sizing, workload management, and credit optimization.
  • Drives a sense of urgency for platform and process improvement to meet and exceed internal and customer data requirements.
  • Applies lean principles to reduce pipeline cycle time and eliminate waste across the data development process.
  • Works with other leaders to standardize data engineering practices, including data modeling, pipeline testing, transformation standards (e.g., dbt), documentation, and reporting on overall platform performance.
  • Reviews and approves data platform releases, schema changes, and deployment plans, ensuring delivery risk is appropriately identified and managed.
  • Leads or supports root cause analysis on significant data quality incidents or pipeline failures in partnership with engineering teams and drives preventive action.

Data Governance, Classification & Audit

  • Owns and matures CSI's data governance framework, including data classification standards (e.g., confidential, PII, non-public personal information), data lineage, cataloging, and retention practices.
  • Serves as a primary point of contact for internal and external audit teams on matters related to data platform controls, access governance, and evidence collection.
  • Partners with Compliance, Risk, and Legal to ensure data governance practices align with applicable regulatory requirements (e.g., GLBA, SOC 2, state privacy laws) and internal policy.
  • Establishes and maintains audit trails, access reviews, and lineage documentation sufficient to support SOC 2 assessments, regulatory exams, and third-party audits.
  • Implements and enforces role-based access control (RBAC) and least-privilege principles across Snowflake and other data platforms.
  • Leads data quality monitoring, issue remediation, and metadata management programs to build organizational trust in reported data.

Operational Performance & Process Improvement

  • Establishes and reviews reporting and dashboards that track departmental priorities, platform reliability, data quality, and goal achievement.
  • Prepares and manages budgets for the data engineering department, including Snowflake and related platform spend, and monitors spend against plan.
  • Leads or contributes to yearly budget and headcount planning for the organization.
  • Ensures appropriate staffing levels, effective workload balance, and scalable data engineering practices across teams.
  • Uses engineering and data metrics/KPIs (e.g., pipeline reliability, data quality, query performance, cost per workload) to measure team performance and drive targeted, continuous improvement actions.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Works closely with product, analytics, data science/AI, and QA teams to define data platform requirements and data-related metrics.
  • Partners with security, risk, and vendor management on due diligence, audit evidence, and response to RFP or security questionnaires as needed.
  • Partners with internal and external audit teams on a recurring basis to support control testing, evidence requests, and remediation of findings.
  • Partners with infrastructure and operations teams as required and appropriate on capacity planning, hosting, and platform reliability.
  • Works effectively with all levels of leadership, including business and customer-facing stakeholders, to support delivery success.
  • Stays current on industry trends, data engineering best practices, and the broader data/analytics stack to support team readiness and capability development.
  • Partners with infrastructure and network teams to resolve technical integration challenges as acquired platforms and data sources are brought into CSI's broader data environment.

People Leadership

  • Leads, mentors, and evaluates managers, including regular 1:1s, goal setting, coaching, and performance review processes.
  • Participates in interviews and hiring decisions for data engineering leadership and key technical roles.
  • Builds high-performing teams that demonstrate accountability, adaptability, and strong employee engagement.
  • Demonstrates a track record of recruiting, developing, and retaining high-quality data engineering talent.

Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Oversees access control processes for data platforms and engineering systems, ensuring appropriate approvals and audit trails.
  • Supports initiatives to reduce reliance on shared credentials and strengthen controls around production and data access.
  • Partners with vendor management on contract review, vendor risk, and cost control for data platform vendors and tools (e.g., Snowflake, ELT/ETL tooling, data catalogs).
  • Owns SOC 2 and other audit or compliance efforts as they relate to data platforms, ensuring timely and complete evidence collection from engineering teams.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 10+ years of relevant experience in data engineering or software engineering, including a strong technical background as an individual contributor on data platforms.
  • Proven, hands-on experience with Snowflake required, including architecture, performance tuning, security model, and cost/credit management.
  • Proven experience managing managers and leading multi-layered data engineering teams in a complex environment.
  • Demonstrated expertise in data governance, data classification, and metadata management practices across large teams.
  • Direct experience supporting internal and external audit engagements, including evidence collection, control testing, and remediation.
  • Strong understanding of Agile methodologies.
  • Demonstrated success recruiting, developing, and retaining high-quality data engineering teams.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to present technical and business information to a wide audience including auditors, customers, peers, and staff.
  • Strong analytical, decision-making, and problem-solving skills; comfortable operating with ambiguity.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in banking, fintech, or financial services, including regulated data environments.
  • Experience with the modern data stack (e.g., Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, Fivetran, or similar ELT/ETL and orchestration tools) and cloud platforms (AWS or Azure).
  • Experience with data catalog and lineage tooling (e.g., Collibra, Alation, Atlan) and classification/tagging frameworks.
  • Familiarity with regulatory and compliance frameworks relevant to banking data (e.g., GLBA, HMDA, SOC 2).
  • Deep experience working with either Atlassian Jira or Azure DevOps to manage data engineering SDLC.
  • Experience driving change across a complex, global engineering organization.
  • Familiarity with vendor management and security or RFP response processes.

What Success Looks Like

  • Engineering teams are well-prepared, supported, and consistently meet delivery expectations.
  • Data platforms deliver secure, high-quality, well-governed data on predictable cadences with continually improving pipeline reliability.
  • Data classification, lineage, and access governance are consistently applied across all data assets.
  • Internal and external audits proceed smoothly, with evidence readily available and findings proactively remediated.
  • The Snowflake environment is optimized for cost, performance, and security.
  • Leadership has clear visibility into data platform priorities, progress, and performance through KPIs and dashboards.
  • CSI's data engineering organization continues to evolve toward a stronger, more resilient, and well-governed data foundation.

title: Delivery Scanner/Toter
description:
Eugene, Oregon, United States of America

Extraordinary Care. Extraordinary Careers.

With one of the nation’s largest, most innovative long-term care pharmacy services providers, there is no limit to the growth of your career.

Managed Healthcare Pharmacy, a Guardian Pharmacy, a member of the Guardian family of pharmacies, has an exciting opportunity for you to join our rapidly growing team in

Eugene, OR.

Why Managed Healthcare Pharmacy? We’re reimagining medication management and transforming care.

Who We Are and What We’re About:

Our core focus is delivering customized medication management solutions to support healthcare organizations serving seniors and individuals with complex care needs. With our comprehensive suite of tech-enabled pharmacy services and a dedicated team of professionals committed to enriching the lives of those we serve, we are redefining how pharmacy care is delivered.

We offer an opportunity to learn and grow your career in a fast-paced, diverse, and inclusive environment. If you are looking for a challenging, team-oriented environment in which you can put your expertise to work, then this is the place for you.

Be the person who helps make sure medications get where they need to go—accurately and on time!

Managed Healthcare Pharmacy is looking for a reliable, organized, and detail-oriented team member to join our delivery team as a Part-Time Delivery Scanner/Toter. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys staying busy, working independently as part of a team, and taking pride in doing things right.

Details

  • Shift: Monday - Friday, starting at 1pm and typically working 4-5 hours

  • Compensation: $17 per hour

  • COMPANY VEHICLE PROVIDED IF MAKING DELIVERIES.

  • Pre-employment drug screening and DMV check are required. CDL not required.

What You’ll Do

Your day starts at 1:00 PM at the pharmacy, preparing medications for our North delivery routes serving Junction City, Corvallis, Albany, Salem, Portland, and surrounding areas.

You’ll:

  • Check medication bubble packs for accuracy.

  • Scan, package, and organize bubble packs.

  • Build individual bags for facilities and nursing stations.

  • Sort completed packages by delivery route.

  • Print and attach packing slips.

  • Organize packages into route-specific baskets.

  • Help load medications for transport to our North route drivers.

  • Work with the pharmacy team to keep everything accurate, organized, and moving on schedule.

  • Comply with all Federal and Company privacy regulations regarding safeguarding of patient information.

Want More Hours?

There may be opportunities to pick up additional hours and responsibilities, including covering the transport run when the regular driver is unavailable or on vacation. Additional route coverage may also be available once the day’s primary duties are completed.

We’re Looking for Someone Who Is:

  • Dependable and punctual.

  • Extremely detail-oriented.

  • Organized and efficient.

  • Comfortable with repetitive tasks that require accuracy.

  • Able to work under pressure and time constraints.

  • A strong team player with a positive attitude.

  • Willing to jump in and help wherever needed.

Why You’ll Love This Job:

You’re not just packing boxes—you’re helping ensure that patients receive the medications they depend on. Your work is an important part of the process that connects our pharmacy with healthcare facilities throughout the region.

Education and/or Certifications:

  • High School Diploma or GED

  • State Driver’s License

Qualifications:

  • Applicants must be 21 years old or older

If you like staying busy, keeping things organized, and being part of a team that makes a real difference, we want to meet you!

Apply today and become an important part of our pharmacy delivery team.

What We Offer:

Guardian provides employees with a comprehensive Total Rewards package, supporting our core value of, “Treat others as you would like to be treated.”

Compensation & Financial

  • Competitive pay
  • 401(k) with company match

Family, Health & Insurance Benefits (Full-Time employees working 30+ hours/week only)

  • Medical, Dental and Vision
  • Health Savings Accounts and Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Company-paid Basic Life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment
  • Company-paid Long-Term Disability and optional Short-Term Disability
  • Voluntary Employee and Dependent Life, Accident and Critical Illness
  • Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts

Wellbeing

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Guardian Angels (Employee assistance fund)

Time Off

  • Paid holidays and sick days
  • Generous vacation benefits based on years of service

The Guardian Difference

Our clients require pharmacy services that aren’t “cookie cutter.” That’s why every Guardian pharmacy is locally operated and empowered with the autonomy to tailor their business to meet their clients’ needs.

Our corporate support offices, based in Atlanta, Ga., provide services such as human resources, business intelligence, legal, and marketing to promote the success of each Guardian location.

Regardless of your role at Guardian, your voice and talents matter. Because healthcare is an ever-changing industry, we encourage innovative thinking, intellectual curiosity, and diverse viewpoints to ensure we stay competitive in today’s dynamic business environment.

At Guardian, we are dedicated to fostering and advancing a diverse and inclusive workforce.

Join us to discover what your best work truly looks like.

title: Commercial and Client Strategy -Assistant Vice President
description:
Who we are looking for

State Street Markets is seeking a high-potential AVP to join the Commercial and Client Strategy team. This role is designed for an ambitious, commercially-minded professional who wants to accelerate their development at the intersection of strategy, sales, and client relationship management. Working directly with the Head of Markets Commercial and Client Strategy, the AVP will help shape and execute initiatives that strengthen client engagement, deepen strategic relationships, and support franchise growth across the Markets product suite. The role offers unique exposure to senior business leaders, top-tier clients, and cross-enterprise initiatives while providing a path to broader responsibilities within Commercial and Client Strategy.This position is ideal for an individual who combines strong analytical capabilities with a genuine interest in understanding clients, building relationships, and helping turn strategic priorities into commercial outcomes.

Why this role is important to us

The Markets' Commercial and Client Strategy team serves as the connective tissue between business strategy, client priorities, and revenue growth. We work across product, sales, relationship management, and business leadership teams to identify opportunities, strengthen client engagement, and drive commercial outcomes. As Markets continues to evolve its client-centric growth strategy, we are building a team that combines strategic thinking with commercial execution. The AVP, Client Engagement will play a critical role in helping the organization become more insight-driven, coordinated, and effective in how we engage our most important clients and prospects.

Beyond the immediate responsibilities, this role is intended to be a development opportunity for future leadership talent within Commercial and Client Strategy.

What you will be responsible for

As Commercial and Client Strategy, Assistant Vice President you will:

  • Partner closely with the Head of Markets Commercial and Client Strategy to support execution of strategic client and commercial priorities across the Markets franchise.

  • Help coordinate and manage engagement plans for key clients, strategic prospects, and priority commercial opportunities.

  • Support the development of client strategies that align Markets capabilities with client needs and business objectives.

  • Conduct research and analysis on client relationships, industry trends, competitive developments, and commercial opportunities.

  • Develop briefing materials, client profiles, meeting preparation documents, and executive-level presentations.

  • Help identify opportunities to deepen client relationships and increase adoption of Markets products and solutions.

  • Track strategic initiatives and ensure follow-through across multiple stakeholders and business partners.

  • Partner with Client Engagement, Client Intelligence, Sales, Product, and Relationship Management teams to translate insights into actionable client plans.

  • Support senior client meetings, industry events, and strategic engagement activities.

  • Build a deep understanding of the Markets product suite, including financing, liquidity, research, and trading solutions.

  • Contribute to the development of scalable client engagement processes, best practices, and management reporting.

  • Serve as a trusted thought partner to the CCS leadership team while gradually assuming ownership of increasingly complex initiatives and client-facing responsibilities.

What we value

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

  • Intellectual curiosity and a desire to learn the business.

  • Strong commercial instincts and interest in client-facing roles.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to build relationships across different levels of the organization.

  • Strong project management and organizational capabilities.

  • Analytical rigor combined with practical business judgment.

  • A proactive, self-starter mindset.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced and evolving environment.

  • Highest standards of professionalism, discretion, and integrity.

Education & Preferred Experience

  • Bachelor's degree required.

  • 4-6 years of experience in financial services, capital markets, business management, sales, client relationship management, strategy or a related field.

  • Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex information into clear recommendations and presentations, proficiency with PowerPoint expected.

  • Familiarity with institutional investing, capital markets, or client-facing financial services environments is preferred.

What success looks like

In your first 12-24 months, you will:

  • Become a trusted extension of the Head of Commercial and Client Strategy.

  • Develop meaningful relationships across Markets leadership, Sales, Product, and client-facing teams.

  • Demonstrate ownership of strategic initiatives and client engagement programs.

  • Build expertise in Markets products, clients, and commercial priorities.

  • Begin assuming responsibility for portions of the client engagement agenda independently.

  • Position yourself for future growth opportunities within Commercial and Client Strategy.

About State Street

What we do. State Street is one of the largest custodian banks, asset managers and asset intelligence companies in the world. From technology to product innovation, we’re making our mark on the financial services industry. For more than two centuries, we’ve been helping our clients safeguard and steward the investments of millions of people. We provide investment servicing, data & analytics, investment research & trading and investment management to institutional clients.

Work, Live and Grow. We make all efforts to create a great work environment. Our benefits packages are competitive and comprehensive. Details vary by location, but you may expect generous medical care, insurance and savings plans, among other perks. You’ll have access to flexible Work Programs to help you match your needs. And our wealth of development programs and educational support will help you reach your full potential.

Inclusion, Diversity and Social Responsibility. We truly believe our employees’ diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives are a powerful contributor to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their maximum potential while adding value to both our organization and our clients. We warmly welcome candidates of diverse origin, background, ability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity and personality. Another fundamental value at State Street is active engagement with our communities around the world, both as a partner and a leader. You will have tools to help balance your professional and personal life, paid volunteer days, matching gift programs and access to employee networks that help you stay connected to what matters to you.

State Street is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer.

Discover more at StateStreet.com/careers

$80,000 - $140,000 Annual

description:

As a global leader in smart, healthy and sustainable buildings, our mission is to reimagine the performance of buildings to serve people, places and the planet. Join a winning team that enables you to build your best future! Our teams are uniquely positioned to support a multitude of industries across the globe. We strive to provide our employees with experience, focused on supporting their physical, financial, and emotional wellbeing. Become a member of the Johnson Controls family and thrive in an empowering company culture where your voice and ideas will be heard – your next great opportunity is just a few clicks away!

Performs or delegates tasks as required to execute and fully complete assigned projects including: hardware design, system programming, installation coordination, system and network commissioning and project closeout. Responsible for the overall financial results of assigned projects including: costs, project billings, and collections. Maintains an effective balance between customer satisfaction and project financial results. Actively pursues selling change orders. Coordinates communication with the customer during all phases of the project. Ensures proper execution of warranty. Validates complete system functionality and resolves issues with subcontractors and others to ensure proper operation. Provides accurate project as-built and commissioning documentation.

    What we look for

  • 2-5 years’ experience with installation and service of fire alarm, access control, CCTV, intrusion and intercom systems
  • Demonstrate working knowledge of electricity and electronics In addition, demonstrate an aptitude for troubleshooting systems and performing necessary repairs
  • Active certifications in access control/CCTV/intrusion/intercom

  • Knowledge of project accounting, costing principals and contracting preferred.

Leads or supports the performance of related assessments to assure compliance to laws, regulations and policies and procedures.

Qualifications

Required

  • Associate degree in Drafting, Engineering Technology, CAD Technology, Manufacturing Technology, or related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  • Strong communication and organizational skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

Preferred

  • Experience with marine, automotive, RV, furniture, upholstery, or seating manufacturing.
  • Experience with CNC cutting systems, routers, nesting software, or CAM programming.

  • Familiarity with bills of material, engineering change management, and production support processes.

Why Join Us?

title: Principal Enterprise Data Management Analyst (Remote)
description:
Who We Are

Join a team that puts its People First! Since 1889, First American (NYSE: FAF) has held an unwavering belief in its people. They are passionate about what they do, and we are equally passionate about fostering an environment where all feel welcome, supported, and empowered to be innovative and reach their full potential. Our inclusive, people-first culture has earned our company numerous accolades, including being named to the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® list for eleven consecutive years. We have also earned awards as a best place to work for women, diversity and LGBTQ+ employees, and have been included on more than 50 regional best places to work lists. First American will always strive to be a great place to work, for all. For more information, please visit www.careers.firstam.com.

What We Do

We are seeking an Enterprise Data Management Analyst - Metadata Mgmt/Data Catalog to help mature enterprise data governance capabilities across metadata management, data discovery, data catalog operations, business glossary, lineage, and governed self-service data use.
This role turns governance standards into practical operating practices. You will work with Data Owners, Data Stewards, Data Custodians, technical teams, Risk, Information Security, and governance partners to improve the completeness, accuracy, usability, and trustworthiness of enterprise metadata. The work is hands-on and cross-functional: you will curate metadata, document lineage, improve glossary content, support catalog adoption, and help stakeholders find, understand, trust, and appropriately use governed data assets.
This is an individual contributor role suited for someone who combines strong documentation and facilitation skills with enough technical fluency to interpret data structures, schemas, data dictionaries, source-to-target mappings, reporting dependencies, and system documentation.

What You Will Do

Metadata, catalog, and governance operations

  • Support enterprise metadata management across priority data domains, applications, systems, reports, data products, and Critical Data Elements (CDEs).
  • Help establish and maintain an authoritative view of what data exists, where it resides, how it is defined, who owns it, and how it is used.
  • Administer, support, and improve data catalog and metadata management content, including catalog records, metadata templates, ownership assignments, classifications, glossary links, lineage documentation, stewardship workflows, and catalog usability.
  • Develop practical procedures, playbooks, templates, intake forms, validation checklists, attestation routines, documentation controls, and operating procedures that make governance repeatable.
  • Partner with business and technology stakeholders to validate business metadata, technical metadata, ownership assignments, glossary terms, CDEs, and lineage completeness.
  • Facilitate onboarding of data sources into governance tooling for scanning, metadata ingestion, catalog publication, and lineage capture.

Glossary, lineage, and metadata quality

  • Develop and maintain business glossary content, including terms, definitions, acronyms, synonyms, data-domain alignment, ownership, and relationships to governed data assets.
  • Facilitate working sessions to resolve inconsistent terminology, conflicting definitions, unclear ownership, and documentation gaps.
  • Document, validate, and maintain lineage for critical data flows, including source-to-target movement, transformations, downstream consumption, reporting dependencies, and business use.
  • Support metadata quality controls by reviewing completeness, consistency, timeliness, ownership, glossary alignment, lineage coverage, and catalog usability.
  • Coordinate review workflows, document discrepancies, escalate unresolved gaps, and help establish sustainable metadata refresh practices.

Stakeholder enablement and reporting

  • Enable federated stewardship by helping Data Owners, Data Stewards, and Data Custodians understand and execute their metadata responsibilities.
  • Prepare operational metrics and reporting for catalog coverage, metadata completeness, glossary coverage, lineage coverage, steward validation, issue aging, adoption, and usage trends.
  • Support governance forums, leadership updates, audit support, risk reviews, and program performance tracking with clear, stakeholder-ready materials.
  • Collaborate across business, technology, analytics, architecture, risk, audit, security, and governance teams to drive alignment without direct authority.

What You Will Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in information systems, computer science, data management, information management, business analytics, library/information science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in metadata management, data cataloging, data governance, enterprise data management, data stewardship, business glossary management, lineage documentation, or closely related work in complex environments.
  • Strong understanding of business metadata, technical metadata, operational metadata, data ownership, stewardship, data domains, CDEs, glossary terms, lineage, and catalog publication.
  • Experience developing procedures, process documentation, operating routines, templates, standards, controls, validation checklists, or governance playbooks.
  • Ability to interpret data structures, schemas, data dictionaries, source-to-target mappings, reporting dependencies, and system documentation.
  • Technical fluency with data architecture, data integration, ETL/ELT concepts, APIs, reporting environments, and metadata ingestion concepts.
  • Strong facilitation, documentation, analytical, stakeholder management, and influencing skills, including the ability to translate technical data concepts into clear business language.
  • Experience producing metrics, KPIs, dashboards, scorecards, status reporting, or operational performance reporting.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Microsoft Purview, Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Atlan, DataHub, BigID, IBM Knowledge Catalog, or similar data catalog, metadata management, governance, or lineage platforms.
  • Working SQL knowledge and experience reviewing data dictionaries, mappings, BI/reporting metadata, lineage, or catalog completeness.
  • Experience in a regulated or highly controlled environment and familiarity with DAMA-DMBOK, CDMP, ISO/IEC 11179, DCAT, or related metadata and data management standards.
  • Experience supporting adjacent data management areas such as data quality, reference/master data, data architecture, BI governance, privacy, security, risk, audit, or regulatory readiness.

Pay Range: $85,000 - $135,000 Annually

This hiring range is a reasonable estimate of the base pay range for this position at the time of posting. Pay is based on a number of factors which may include job-related knowledge, skills, experience, business requirements and geographic location.

What We Offer

By choice, we don’t simply accept individuality – we embrace it, we support it, and we thrive on it! Our People First culture is inclusive for all employees - not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it's the key to our success. We are proud to foster an authentic and inclusive workplace For All. You are free and encouraged to bring your entire, unique self to work. First American is an equal opportunity employer in every sense of the term.

Based on eligibility, First American offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401k, PTO/paid sick leave and other great benefits like an employee stock purchase plan.

title: Market Data Reporting & Analytics, AVP
description:
Who we are looking for
Responsible for managing market data financial operations, including invoice reconciliation, spend reporting, financial governance, and process improvement initiatives. Manages and maintains supplier, contract, and financial data within Optimize Spend (FITS) to ensure accuracy and data integrity. Ensures market data expenses are accurately validated against contractual commitments, invoices are processed in a timely manner, and reporting obligations are completed accurately. Partners with Procurement, Finance, Account Management, vendors, and business stakeholders to support operational excellence and financial transparency.

What you will be responsible for

  • Maintain supplier, contract, and market data inventory records within Optimize Spend (FITS) to ensure data accuracy and completeness.
  • Perform data quality reviews of Optimize Spend (FITS) records, identifying and resolving missing, inaccurate or outdated information.
  • Generate and analyze reports from Optimize Spend (FITS) to support spend reporting.
  • Identify opportunities to improve Optimize Spend (FITS) processes, reporting capabilities, and data management practices through automation and standardization.
  • Manage the end-to-end invoice reconciliation process, ensuring vendor invoices are validated against contractual terms and supporting documentation.
  • Maintain ownership of assigned billing accounts and drive timely completion of reconciliation activities.
  • Prepare and review invoice walks and reconciliation packages for approval and payment processing.
  • Track and support Financial Case governance activities, ensuring savings and avoidance initiatives are appropriately documented.
  • Collaborate with Sourcing, Account Management, vendors and business partners to resolve invoice and contract issues.
  • Identify opportunities for process improvements and automation to increase efficiency and reduce manual effort.
  • Assist with project work, including remediation efforts, operational initiatives, and special assignments.
  • Maintain strong relationships with internal stakeholders and external vendors.

What we value

These skills will help you succeed in this role

  • Proficient in Optimize Spend (FITS)
  • Ability to build strong relationships with businesses, procurement, and vendors
  • Strong communication skills both verbal and written
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort with data manipulation, financial modeling, reconciliation
  • Strong MS Office skills – Excel, Access, Powerpoint, Word
  • Project management experience
  • Market Data product knowledge and experience preferred
  • Strong Attention to Detail and Organizational Skills

Education & Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing market data vendor invoices, contract reconciliation, spend reporting, financial governance, and operational controls.
  • Hands-on experience with Optimize Spend (FITS) or similar market data inventory, expense management, or procurement platforms.

  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including pivot tables, formulas, data analysis, and reporting. Experience with Access, PowerPoint, Power BI, Tableau, or other reporting tools is preferred.
  • Proven ability to drive process improvements, automation initiatives, and operational efficiency programs.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a deadline-driven environment.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively present information to senior management and business stakeholders.
  • Strong attention to detail and a commitment to data accuracy, financial controls, and governance standards, while demonstrating a proactive, self-motivated approach and the ability to work independently and collaborate effectively across global teams.
  • Experience within a global financial institution and/or market data procurement organization is strongly preferred.
  • Preferred understanding of market data products, licensing models, exchange fees, and vendor billing practices, along with knowledge of financial markets, investment products, trading platforms, and market data consumption practices.

title: Sr. Field Service Engineer
description:
We begin with dreams. Dreams drive our motivation. Dreams are our future. The world's dreams, people's dreams, our dreams. Our passion creates ideas that make dreams come alive. Technology and products that were only dreams become reality.


All for dreams. Dreams challenge and the Nidec-Group will continue to meet the challenge. For the world's and people's tomorrows; the world's first, the world's best technologies and products; we will continue our part in creating a better society.

Job Summary

Nidec is the world's No.1 comprehensive motor and drive manufacturer handling "everything that spins and moves", miniature to gigantic. Nidec is a global enterprise comprised of over 300 subsidiaries/affiliates. We are a leading manufacturer of commercial motors, industrial motors, appliance motors, and controls. Nidec motors can be found in products that range from cell phones, computers and home appliances to industrial and mining equipment – and everything in between. Our product line features a full line of high efficiency motors for industrial applications in water treatment, mining, oil and gas, and power generation, and for commercial applications such as pool and spa, condensers, cooling towers and large refrigeration units.

From keeping us comfortable in our homes to pumping clean water to making our cars more safe, electric motors are an indispensable part of our daily lives. At Nidec, our employees are on the forefront of developing new motor technologies. As we move deeper into the age of robotics, the impact of motors will only increase.

With over 140,000 employees stationed worldwide, Nidec continues to be a unique organization, and each location maintains its individual personality.

Job Description

The Field Service Engineer V supports customers and internal teams by performing routine, well‑defined service tasks in field environments. The role works closely with senior field service engineers, service coordinators, and technical support teams, following established procedures and safety standards. Success is demonstrated through accurate execution of service activities, effective communication with customers, and steady development of field service engineering capability.

Responsibilities

  • Installation and commissioning, troubleshooting, repairs, and predictive/preventative maintenance of automated systems and power conversion products/assemblies independently or as part of a team on larger projects
  • Work with motors, generators, drives, plant automation and power quality systems
  • Work with a variety of PLC’s including Rockwell, Emerson, GE, Schneider, and Beckhoff
  • Work with a variety of HMI software including Factory Talk, Proficy View, Wonderware, Vijeo Designer, and others
  • Provide hands-on, on-site training to customers
  • Work with and configure industrial networks
  • Work closely with in-house engineers on project design and testing of drive systems
  • Display professionalism, proactively interface, and effectively communicate with the customer to build and maintain a high level of customer satisfaction
  • Provide telephone, email, and other support to customers
  • When required, participate in paid, rotating after hours phone duty for customer remote support and breakdown assistance
  • Participate in supporting after-service sales activities such as proposing added services, spare parts, and additional upgrades
  • Provide emergency field service for customers on an as needed basis
  • Maintain working knowledge of safety policies and regulations to ensure duties of self and others are performed in a safe manner

Learning Period

  • Formal training at the Cleveland office and on-site training with a senior FSE when needed
  • Expectation to work independently within 9-12 months

Working Conditions

  • Position requires approximately 60% travel in the field
  • Approximately 60% of above travel will be in an assigned region
  • Remaining travel will be supporting customers in other regions of North America and occasionally worldwide.
  • Requires some travel short notice for emergency repairs
  • May require extended hours or longer trips for start-ups and emergency repairs
  • Work from regional “home” office when not on the road
  • Considerable amount of walking required
  • May require climbing of staircases and access ladders, working at heights, in tight spaces, outdoors in hot and cold weather, and lifting up to 70 lbs
  • Field work requires wearing and working in appropriate safety gear
  • Carry service bag (25-50 lbs.), laptop case/caddy, as well as other trade tools
  • Negotiate and navigate airports, airports concourses, and parking garages



Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Two-year associate degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Technology, Military Technical Training Program, or related field
  • Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering or Engineering Technology preferred
  • Valid Driver’s License required to drive to customer locations, either from airports or Cleveland office
  • Must be able to pass a federal background check
  • Minimum of five (5) years prior experience in an industrial automation (i.e. metals, pulp & paper, marine, cranes, mining) or renewable energy environment required
  • Thorough knowledge of analog and digital circuits, configuration of AC/DC drives, AC/DC Motor Theory, PLC’s, and HMI’s
  • Experience using electronic test equipment such as Data Recorders, DMM’s, Clamp-on ammeters, Megaohmmeters, and Oscilloscopes
  • Experience in troubleshooting power electronics circuitry desirable
  • Experience with Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), Grid-Tie Solar Inverters, or EV charging is desirable but not required
  • Experience with Nidec low voltage drives including AD3000 & AD5000, Accel500, Unidrive M, Answer Drives DC, ADDVANTAGE-32, and Mentor MP is desirable but not required
  • Ability to work independently, resolve technical and manufacturing issues without detailed direction, and work as part of a team
  • Ability to work within strict deadlines
  • Ability to use hand and/or power tools
  • Ability to read Electrical Drawings/Schematics
  • Competent in Microsoft Office software programs
  • Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills
  • Outstanding verbal and written communications skills

Additional Job Details

title: Data Engineer III - Partner Data
description:
At Expedia Group, we help travelers explore the world, one journey at a time. As a global travel company powered by passionate people, trusted partnerships, and leading technology, we connect travelers, partners, and advertisers through our consumer brands, B2B network, and travel advertising business.


Here, you'll do meaningful work that helps millions of people discover, book, and experience travel with more ease, confidence, and joy. Our five Behaviors-Traveler First, Think Big, Operate with Excellence, Ownership Mindset, and Succeed Together-help foster a supportive environment where people can grow their careers and have the flexibility, benefits, and support to do their best work. Join us and build for travelers everywhere.

Introduction to the Team

Partner Data Team at EG builds innovative products, services, and tools to deliver high-quality data experiences for partners and our internal teams. A singular technology platform powered by data and machine learning provides secure, differentiated, and personalized experiences for our partners that drive customer satisfaction.

As a Data Engineer, you will lead projects, design and build scalable, reliable data services and pipelines by leveraging AI tools and technologies that power analytics, reporting, and data-driven product experiences. You will combine strong software engineering fundamentals with data engineering and AI skills to deliver secure, high-quality data products on modern cloud infrastructure.

In this role, you will:

  • Own and evolve complex, business‑critical data products end to end — from technical design and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and day‑to‑day production support, escalating appropriately on the most complex or cross‑org decisions

  • Apply modern engineering practices and use AI as a co‑pilot across the software development lifecycle to clarify requirements, explore designs, accelerate coding, strengthen automated testing, and improve operational excellence and reliability

  • Collaborate with partners across engineering, product, data, and business functions — contributing to cross‑team designs, surfacing trade‑offs clearly, and helping align simple, resilient solutions

  • Design and integrate services, APIs, and data models so that high‑quality data and capabilities are easily consumable by both human users and AI systems, working within established architectural patterns and guardrail

  • Share knowledge and mentor others, especially earlier‑career engineers, through code reviews, pairing, and design discussions — including helping teammates use AI tools effectively and responsibly as part of their daily workflow

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science or a related technical field; or Equivalent related professional experience

  • 5+ years of relevant professional experience

  • Experience with owning data products, with demonstrated impact within a domain or product

  • Proven experience delivering at least one significant end to end service or product within a product or domain using AI tools(like Claude, Codex, copilot).

  • Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (like Java, Scala) and strong computer science fundamentals (data structures, algorithms, object-oriented or functional design), with hands-on experience in system design (LLD), API design, and data modeling

  • Experience working with data pipelines, batch and stream, including building, consuming, and evolving them.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience designing and building reliable, scalable systems on cloud platforms, including contributing to service boundaries, resilience mechanisms, and operational best practices

  • Strong proficiency using AI tools and techniques as part of everyday software engineering work (for example, exploring implementation options, generating and hardening code, enhancing test coverage, or analyzing production behavior), with sound judgment about when human‑only review is required

  • Experience developing frameworks for AI-driven coding agents, including MCP and spec-driven development methodologies

  • Experience defining and enforcing AI governance practices to ensure responsible, secure, and compliant AI system development

  • Experience with big data technologies like Spark, Kafka, Flink and no-SQL data stores like Cassandra, Scylla and Iceberg.

  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate and influence across disciplines — partnering with engineering, product, and data stakeholders to move designs forward, unblock dependencies, and land changes that span multiple teams

  • Track record of leading technical workstreams that simplify components or services, improve performance or reliability, or increase developer productivity within and adjacent to your team

The total cash range for this position in Austin is $146,000.00 to $204,500.00. Employees in this role have the potential to increase their pay up to $233,500.00, which is the top of the range, based on ongoing, demonstrated, and sustained performance in the role.


Starting pay for this role will vary based on multiple factors, including location, available budget, and an individual’s knowledge, skills, and experience. Pay ranges may be modified in the future.


Benefits and perks

Expedia Group offers benefits and perks designed to support employees and their families, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, an Employee Assistance Program, wellness and travel reimbursement, travel discounts, and International Airlines Travel Agent Network (IATAN) membership. Expedia Group includes three flagship consumer brands - Expedia, Hotels.com, and Vrbo - along with a leading B2B travel business and travel advertising offerings. Across our brands and business, we help travelers explore the world with confidence and ease.
